THE CAPTAIN JUMPED SHIP. THE SHIP ISN'T TAKING ON WATER YET.

MongoDB CEO CJ Desai resigned Monday, less than a year into the job, to run Meta's new enterprise AI unit. The stock fell 18.5% to close at $334.68, its worst day since March. Per the company's release, the business is unchanged: Q3 and full-year guidance kept as is, and Dev Ittycheria, who took the company from $35 million to $2.3 billion in revenue between 2014 and 2025, is back as interim CEO. The timing is bad because Tuesday is its investor day at Nasdaq, and Guggenheim says this drop could be an attractive entry point.

My thesis: a database sells through developers, not through its CEO. Meta going after the man running MongoDB for enterprise AI is a good grade for the product, not a weakness of the company. With guidance still standing, most of this 18% is shock.

So I count this selloff as an opportunity: if Ittycheria reiterates full-year guidance at investor day today, I'm thinking of buying a first lot of $MDB. If he pulls guidance, I won't even look at it.

Idea source: Barron's — Kit Norton, "MongoDB Stock Sinks 18%. Why the CEO Departure Timing Is Bad for the Stock."
Data source: MongoDB release, September 28, 2026

@grok @elonmusk @jgebbia @grok , Technical Note — Lead Poisoning Flow & Eagle Sentinel Pilot Intervention**

**Purpose**  
This note maps the six-step lead-poisoning pathway in bald eagles to the ground-based, drone-free detection and response functions of the Eagle Sentinel Pilot. The goal is earlier identification of compromised raptors and contaminated sites so rehab partners can intervene before mortality.

**Pathway (Steps 1–5)**  
1. **Source** — Lead fragments from ammunition in carcasses and gut piles.  
2. **Ingestion** — Eagles scavenge contaminated remains.  
3. **Absorption** — Gastric acid dissolves lead into blood.  
4. **Distribution & Effects** — Anemia, weakness, nerve damage, seizures, organ failure; lead sequestered in bone.  
5. **Impact** — Elevated mortality and slowed population growth.

**Intervention Layer (Step 6) — Eagle Sentinel Pilot**

| Function | Specification | Role in the lead pathway |
|---|---|---|
| Thermal imaging | \~600 m range | Detects grounded, hypothermic, or inactive raptors that can no longer thermoregulate or fly — common late-stage lead presentation. |
| Acoustic arrays | \~350 m distress-call range | Captures abnormal vocalization and reduced activity associated with weakness and neurological impairment. |
| Environmental probes | Lead threshold >0.2 ppm plus air/soil context | Flags contaminated feeding zones so responders can prioritize search grids and reduce further ingestion. |
| Bio-mimetic cameras | 20 MP ground-level verification | Confirms identity and condition without aerial disturbance. |
| Swarm-like ground sensor units | Dynamic coverage; target 99% over \~2,000 km² | Maintains persistent watch in wetland and forest terrain where scavenged carcasses concentrate. |
| Multi-modal AI + federated learning | Target >95% fusion accuracy; low-latency local inference | Combines thermal, acoustic, and environmental signals to score “grounded / distressed / possible toxicosis” events. |
| Secure MQTT + Starlink Direct-to-Cell | Encrypted relay; target <1 s wide-area handoff | Delivers alerts to rehab and field teams when a bird is still recoverable. |
| Private mobile app | Real-time alerts, heatmaps, validated community input | Routes TEAM OWL / field responders to coordinates; logs outcomes for model improvement. |

**Operational intent**  
The Pilot does not remove lead from the landscape. It shortens the time between **clinical decline** (Steps 4–5) and **human intervention** (capture, chelation, rehab). Parallel environmental readings support targeted prevention messaging (non-lead ammunition, burial of gut piles) without requiring aerial platforms.

**Constraints**  
Ground-only. No drones. Respects Coast Salish Traditional Territory protocols. Sensitive site names are withheld from public materials.

**Pilot frame**  
Fraser River Delta, Delta, BC — target launch Q4 2026.  
Field baseline (project record): 19 years; 190 live rescues; 520 documented deaths; \~70% lead-associated.

**Developed by** Mark MiLan with assisted research by Grok (xAI)

items.text:
Our latest paper: "Adapt the Physics, Not the Weights"

World models will be deployed into a physical world that isn't static. Viscosity changes with temperature, friction with wear, mass with payload. A learned world model can carry those parameters in three places: in its weights, inferred from context, or as an explicit input.

We tested all three on a turbulent flow after the parameter drifted past training. All three fell well short.

After a 25% change in Reynolds number, the share of the best achievable forecast:
• In the weights: 16%
• Inferred from context: 53%
• Handed the true new value as an input: 67%
• Physics solver + small learned residual, identifying the value itself from 11 noisy frames: 97%

The network knows the parameter. The physics knows what to do with it.

Across -10% to +40% drift, the hybrid keeps 92-98% accuracy. Its learned part is 7x smaller than the network it beats, trained once at a single condition, then frozen. Even trained across the new condition and handed the true value, the network reaches 83%.

Why it matters: the default fix for a world model facing changing conditions is to give the network the parameter or train it on more conditions. That makes it aware of the parameter, not able to use it. Where a parameter's effect follows a known law, supplying the law beats learning it from examples.

What's new:
1. A head-to-head measurement of every place a network can carry a drifting parameter, against physics in the loop, scored by forecast horizon in a chaotic flow with the drift outside training.
2. Physics alone isn't the answer either. A solver missing one real effect fits the parameter wrong (Re 38.8 for a true 50) and loses 84% of the forecast. A correction learned once, at one condition, removes that bias.
3. A warning that needs no ground truth. When what the network learned itself drifts, the hybrid fails (38%), and the identified parameter slides as the observation window grows. A deployed system can see its own split between physics and learning break.

The design principle: put the law of what drifts in the dynamics, identify it at run time, and learn only what doesn't drift. (FYI, this is precisely what Niva's Manifold AI does).

It's one flow with full-field observations, so this is a principle to test, not a proof. Next: whether it needs a full solver or only the drifting law in explicit form.

Pre-registered, fresh data, three seeds.

Arxiv: soon
Currently: https://t.co/TsqaC9XOYw

items.text:
51.3% of the token budget to match the final pretraining loss of a model that ran the full course. 1.95x equivalent convergence speed. A final loss 0.091 below the official baseline. And it topped HuggingFace Daily Papers without any splashy launch.

Shanghai AI Laboratory and Shanghai Jiao Tong University (LUMIA Lab) present NCP-ArchPreview, the world's first 8.9B discrete latent-space foundation model.

It breaks the single dogma of pure Next-Token Prediction by introducing "Next Concept Prediction" (NCP) as a new pretraining task — predicting high-level concepts in a discrete latent space rather than the next raw token. Trained on Dolmo-3's 5.73T open-source corpus, it mirrors the shift from pixel space to latent space that transformed image generation with Latent Diffusion, and the JEPA-style insight that predicting high-level representations beats reconstructing low-level details. In Stage-1 it uses only 51.3% of the token budget to match OLMo-3-7B's full-run final loss; in Stage-2 annealing convergence reaches 1.51x the baseline.

Result: NCP-ArchPreview shows that latent-space language models can nearly halve pretraining token consumption while converging faster and lower — a potential first brick of future AI, per overseas reviewers. Weights and code are open.

NCP-ArchPreview Technical Report: Moving towards Latent Space Language Models through Next Concept Prediction
